Feeds in grasslands and agriculture fields; nesting habitat components include open accessible water with dense tall emergent vegetation, a protected nesting substrate (including flooded or Tricolored blackbird –/ST Unlikely CAFSD Indirect thorny vegetation), and a suitable nearby foraging space with Agelaius tricolor adequate insect prey. Relies on groundwater dependent ecosystems for breeding and roosting (Rohde et al 2019). No listed occurrences in management areas, outside of the species’ range (eBird 2020). Barren to sparsely vegetated beaches, barrier beaches, saltevaporation pond levees, and shores of alkali lakes; also nests on Western snowy plover gravel bars in rivers with wide flood plains; needs sandy, gravelly, Charadrius alexandrinus –/SSC Likely CNDDB Indirect or friable soils for nesting
